questions.questionText: Which of the following is a balanced chemical equation for the reaction of hydrogen with oxygen to form water?
questions.explanation: Balanced equation has equal atoms on both sides. Option B satisfies this.

questions.questionText: The reaction: 2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂ is an example of:
questions.explanation: PbO is reduced to Pb and C is oxidized to CO₂, so it is a redox reaction.

questions.questionText: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler substances is called:
questions.explanation: Decomposition reaction involves breaking down into simpler substances.

questions.questionText: When iron nails are placed in copper sulphate solution, the colour changes from blue to:
questions.explanation: Iron displaces copper forming FeSO₄ solution which is green.

questions.questionText: Which is a double displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: NaOH and HCl exchange ions to form NaCl and H₂O.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reactions is a combination reaction?
questions.hint: Two reactants combine to form one product.
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide combines with water to form calcium hydroxide.

questions.questionText: What happens when magnesium ribbon is burnt in air?
questions.optionB: It burns with dazzling white flame
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame forming magnesium oxide.

questions.questionText: Which gas is evolved when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Hydrogen gas is released.

questions.questionText: The insoluble substance formed in a precipitation reaction is called:
questions.explanation: An insoluble solid formed during reaction is called precipitate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents oxidation?
questions.explanation: Oxidation is addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen.

questions.questionText: The reaction in which heat is absorbed is called:
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat.

questions.questionText: Rancidity can be prevented by:
questions.explanation: Antioxidants prevent oxidation of fats and oils.

questions.questionText: Which is a thermal decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating.

questions.questionText: In the reaction MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂, which substance is oxidized?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions from HCl lose electrons to form chlorine gas.

questions.questionText: Copper powder turns black on heating because:
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with oxygen to form black copper oxide.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an exothermic process?
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy in the form of heat.

questions.questionText: What type of reaction is represented by AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃?
questions.explanation: The ions exchange partners forming AgCl precipitate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is reduced in the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O?
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen to form copper, hence it is reduced.

questions.questionText: Food packets are flushed with nitrogen gas to:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen prevents oxidation of oils and fats.

questions.questionText: Which reaction occurs when electricity is passed through acidified water?
questions.explanation: Electric current decomposes water into hydrogen and oxygen.

tests.title: Chemical Reactions – Test 3 (Corrosion, Oxidation States & Analysis)

questions.questionText: The green coating that appears on copper vessels over time is due to:
questions.hint: Corrosion of copper in moist air with CO₂.
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with CO₂ and moisture to form basic copper carbonate (Cu(OH)₂·CuCO₃), which is green.

questions.questionText: What is the oxidation state of manganese in MnO₂?
Which of the following is NOT a physical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting involves a chemical reaction forming iron oxide — a new substance — so it is a chemical change.

questions.questionText: In the reaction 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, what type of reaction is this?
questions.hint: One reactant breaks into simpler products.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen — a classic decomposition reaction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines a reducing agent?
questions.optionB: A substance that loses electrons and gets oxidized
questions.optionC: A substance that causes reduction in another and itself gets oxidized
questions.hint: Think about what the reducing agent does to the other reactant.
questions.explanation: A reducing agent reduces another substance and is itself oxidized in the process.

questions.questionText: Silver articles turn black over time due to formation of:
questions.hint: Reaction with sulphur compounds in air.
questions.explanation: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) in air to form black silver sulphide (Ag₂S).

questions.questionText: Photosynthesis can be represented as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Energy is absorbed; oxidation states also change.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs light energy (endothermic) and involves oxidation of water and reduction of CO₂ (redox).

questions.questionText: When sodium hydroxide reacts with hydrochloric acid, the reaction is:
questions.explanation: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O is a neutralisation reaction, which is a type of double displacement.

questions.questionText: Which condition is required for the decomposition of silver chloride?
questions.explanation: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ occurs in sunlight. This photolytic decomposition is used in photography.

questions.questionText: In the thermite reaction: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, which substance acts as the oxidising agent?
questions.hint: Which substance causes oxidation of the other?
questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃ oxidises Al (Al gets oxidised to Al₂O₃) and is itself reduced to Fe. So Fe₂O₃ is the oxidising agent.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs shows both a combination and an exothermic reaction?
questions.hint: Haber process — industrial synthesis of ammonia.
questions.explanation: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ is a combination reaction (two reactants → one product) and releases heat (exothermic).

questions.questionText: A student adds dilute H₂SO₄ to zinc granules. Which observation confirms the reaction is a displacement?
questions.optionC: Evolution of a colourless gas that burns with a pop sound
questions.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. H₂ gas is colourless and burns with a pop sound — confirming displacement of hydrogen by zinc.

questions.questionText: During electrolysis of water, the ratio of volume of hydrogen to oxygen collected at electrodes is:
questions.explanation: From the balanced equation, 2 moles of H₂ are produced for every 1 mole of O₂, giving a 2:1 volume ratio.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about a balanced chemical equation?
questions.optionA: Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
questions.optionB: Number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides
questions.optionC: Number of molecules is always equal on both sides
questions.optionD: It obeys the law of conservation of mass
questions.hint: Atoms are conserved, but molecules may not be.
questions.explanation: Balancing conserves atoms and mass, not necessarily the number of molecules. E.g. 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 3 molecules on left and 2 on right.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): When a strip of copper is placed in silver nitrate solution, the solution turns blue.
Reason (R): Copper displaces silver from silver nitrate solution and copper nitrate is formed.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.optionB: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.optionC: A is true but R is false
questions.optionD: A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Copper displaces silver; the blue colour is due to Cu(NO₃)₂ in solution. Both A and R are correct and causally linked.

questions.questionText: Quicklime (CaO) reacts with water vigorously and releases heat. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.explanation: CaO and H₂O combine to form one product Ca(OH)₂ (combination) and heat is released (exothermic).

questions.questionText: Which of the following best explains why chips manufacturers flush bags with nitrogen gas?
questions.optionC: Nitrogen is inert and prevents oxidation of fats in chips
questions.optionD: Nitrogen increases shelf life by killing bacteria
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is chemically inert. It displaces oxygen in the packet, preventing oxidation of oils/fats and hence preventing rancidity.

questions.questionText: The reaction between barium chloride and sodium sulphate produces a white precipitate of barium sulphate. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Both ions exchange partners; insoluble product forms.
questions.explanation: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl. Ions exchange (double displacement) and BaSO₄ precipitates out of solution.

questions.questionText: Which change in oxidation number correctly identifies the reducing agent in: H₂ + CuO → Cu + H₂O?
questions.optionA: Cu changes from +2 to 0; Cu is the reducing agent
questions.optionB: H changes from 0 to +1; H₂ is the reducing agent
questions.optionC: O changes from -2 to 0; CuO is the reducing agent
questions.optionD: H changes from +1 to 0; H₂O is the reducing agent
questions.hint: Reducing agent gets oxidised — its oxidation number increases.
questions.explanation: H in H₂ goes from 0 to +1 (oxidised). H₂ loses electrons, causing reduction of CuO, so H₂ is the reducing agent.

questions.questionText: A precipitate of lead iodide (yellow) is formed when lead nitrate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution. Which type of reaction is this?
questions.hint: Pb²⁺ and I⁻ exchange from their respective compounds.
questions.explanation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂↓ + 2KNO₃. The cations and anions exchange partners — a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.
